messages.text: Ok design such a forward calorimeter and fit it into the two layouts.

I’ll design the tungsten–quartz FCAL as an isolated prototype and integrate it into both layout drawings. I’ll include readout, supports and services, and check the depth and acceptance available in each layout.

I’m using the project’s coordination and design-evidence workflows. I’ll have CaloTech develop the sampling and readout details, and SysArch assess the two layout interfaces, while I build the parameterized geometry checks and drawings. A separate PhysVal review will assess the resulting evidence.

The design is converging on tungsten with longitudinal quartz fibres and a compact rear SiPM readout. This avoids CASTOR’s bulky side light guides. Long and short fibre populations will provide two shower-depth measurements; extracting separate EM and hadronic energies will require calibration.

I’m proposing a 50 mm physical bore, reduced from the draft 80 mm reservation, so η = 5 rays enter at the front. The current beam pipe ends at 4 m, so that change remains conditional on the downstream machine interface.

The proposed package is 1.8 m long: a 1.2 m sampling block followed by optical fan-out, sensors, cooling and service connections. The preliminary material calculation gives more than ten nuclear interaction lengths along a full-depth path; that does not establish shower containment.

The local simulation environment has changed since its last recorded check. I’m rechecking its availability before attempting native geometry validation.

The common FCAL body fits both layouts. The interface checks also found an EM gap in layout 02 between the narrow FCAL and the LAr endcap, so I’m adding a short, wider tungsten–quartz collar in its reserved space.

That collar needs a small service neck beside the FCAL. I’ll include its clearance to the cryostat and HCAL explicitly in the fit checks.

The analytical geometry checks pass, including finite fibre placement, readout packing, bore and sensor intrusion controls, material accounting, and negative-side symmetry. The body contains 24,324 fibre passages per end and 96 long/short tower outputs.

I’m now running the ROOT geometry checks and generating the integrated views for both layouts.

The ROOT checks pass for both sides of both layouts, including the layout-02 collar and service neck, with no overlaps at the 10⁻⁵ mm tolerance. Independent boundary traces agree with the analytical material paths.

The remaining limits are optical response, radiation lifetime, shower containment and engineering qualification. I’m retaining the weak transition regions and clamshell seams in the evidence for review.

Both layout drawings and the design dossier are ready. The independent review has confirmed that the retained native evidence matches the source revision and is checking the fit and coverage claims. I’m finishing the validation records and draft PR.

The draft is open as PR #88. The independent review found no blocking issue with the scoped prototype fit; I’ve corrected its two minor documentation findings.

CI caught a journal metadata error in the review record. I’m fixing that record and checking the final PR validations before handing it over.

Linux passed all ten geometry tests, but its regenerated report differs from the Mac-generated file in the exact text comparison. I’m checking numerical serialization and making the report portable while keeping the exact snapshot check and geometry tolerances intact.

The corrected report now passes on Linux. The independent review confirmed that the change affects only report formatting; the model, inputs, native evidence and tolerances are unchanged. The broader repository validation is still running.

The design and fit checks are complete, including the additional EM collar needed for layout 02. The independent review found no blockers within the prototype scope; I’m finishing the review record and waiting for the broader repository checks.

Both layouts now have parameterized placement drawings. The common body is 1.8 m long, with radii of 50–290 mm; layout 02 also needs a 440 mm EM collar. The design records the bore reduction and added service space explicitly. ROOT found no overlaps in the modeled assemblies, while machine clearance, optical response and engineering qualification remain open.
The draft PR is updated and the working tree is clean. Its FCAL checks and journal build have passed; the broader repository run is still working through the existing geometry tests.

Designed and fitted as a **prototype** in [draft PR #88](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/88), documented in **DES-039 / ADR-010**.

The common unit uses tungsten with quartz fibres and rear SiPM readout: **1.8 m long, inner/outer radii 50/290 mm**, with 96 optical signals per end.

| Layout | Body position, both ends | Additional component |
|---|---|---|
| [01 drawing]([redacted] | \|z\| = 4.533–6.333 m | — |
| [02 drawing]([redacted] | \|z\| = 4.850–6.650 m | 440 mm EM collar |

Eleven FCAL controls pass. ROOT found zero overlaps in the modeled assemblies, and 90 material-path controls agreed with analytical calculations. Broader repository CI is still running.

The fit requires the documented **R80 → R50 bore amendment and added service allocations**. Machine clearance, optical/shower performance and engineering qualification remain open; production integration awaits review.
